aspects.says: A method declared in a class or inherited from a superclass wins over an interface default, even when called through the interface; the default is reached with X.super.m().
basis: section:A Class Method Beats a Default, a More Specific Interface Beats Its Parent, and Any Other Conflict Is Yours to Resolve

aspects.says: A class open to subclassing keeps the sequence and its rules in a final method and lets subclasses fill in protected hooks, so no subclass can skip the rules and no caller can run a step on its own.
basis: section:A Class Open to Subclassing Needs a Final Skeleton and Protected Hooks; Otherwise Make It final

aspects.says: A default the superclass inherits is still a default, so it conflicts with an unrelated default the subclass inherits, and the class doesn't compile until it overrides the method.
basis: section:A Class Method Beats a Default, a More Specific Interface Beats Its Parent, and Any Other Conflict Is Yours to Resolve

aspects.says: Adding a default to a published interface can conflict with an implementer's other interface: its source stops compiling, and a class file compiled earlier loads but throws IncompatibleClassChangeError at the call.
basis: section:Adding a Default Method Can Break Implementers: Their Source Stops Compiling and Their Old Class Files Fail at the Call

aspects.says: The skeleton's rules include what happens when a hook throws, so its cleanup goes in a finally.
basis: section:A Class Open to Subclassing Needs a Final Skeleton and Protected Hooks; Otherwise Make It final

aspects.says: A subclass is usable wherever its superclass is, so callers can use every inherited public method on it, including ones that bypass the subclass's own rules.
basis: section:A Subclass Can Be Used Wherever Its Superclass Is, So It Inherits Every Promise the Superclass Makes
